title: HB 5101 (89R): Relating to the cancellation of all voter registrations following each presidential election; making conforming changes to voter registration and maintenance procedures; imposing a civil penalty.
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id) not stated.
(b_no_id_remedy) not stated.
(c_mail_ballot_id) not stated.
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(other) Sec 1 (13.142(c)): initial registration certificate expires on the November 30 immediately following the next presidential election.
(other) Sec 2-3: certificate contents and notice (renewal certificate references removed).
(other) Sec 4-6 (15.052(a), 15.081(a), 16.032): confirmation notice and suspense list wording; cancellation after the first (not second) general election after listing.
(other) Sec 7 (16.039): civil penalty up to $5,000 per failure by a registrar; secretary of state shall withhold funds.
(other) Sec 8 (adds 16.040): on November 30 following a presidential election the registrar shall cancel all voter registrations; not challengeable; re-registration under Chapter 13.
(other) Sec 9: right to challenge cancellation does not apply to 16.040 cancellations.
(other) Sec 10: repeal of Chapter 14 (renewal of registration).
(other) Sec 11-12: applies to certificates applied for on or after September 1, 2025; effective September 1, 2025.
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
